subproblem.title: Sector points a + l·e (small l > 0) of positive density lie in spt C
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, C ∈ 𝒟_2(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ 2) with IsIntegerMultiplicity C, a, e ∈ ℝ^P, δ > 0 and k ∈ ℕ with k ≥ 1, and assume HasMassDensity C (t(cos φ·a + sin φ·e)) k for all t > 0 and all φ with 0 < φ < δ. Then there is l₀ > 0 such that a + l·e ∈ spt C (C.support) for every l with 0 < l < l₀.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) 2) (a e : Euclid P) (δ : ℝ) (k : ℕ), IsIntegerMultiplicity C → 0 < δ → 1 ≤ k → (∀ t φ : ℝ, 0 < t → 0 < φ → φ < δ → HasMassDensity C (t • (Real.cos φ • a + Real.sin φ • e)) k) → ∃ l₀ : ℝ, 0 < l₀ ∧ ∀ l : ℝ, 0 < l → l < l₀ → a + l • e ∈ C.support
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 (sector points of density k ≥ 1 lie in spt C) and the polar-coordinate computation of step 2(d) (y_j = a + λ_j e = t_j(cos φ_j a + sin φ_j e)) of the parent proof, specialised to σ = 0, u = 1. Notation: ω_2 := unitBallVolume 2; B_ρ(y) open ball.
1. (Choice of l₀.) Take l₀ := δ > 0. Fix l with 0 < l < δ.
2. (Polar form of a + l·e.) Put t := √(1 + l²) > 0 and φ := arctan l. Since l > 0, φ > 0 (Real.arctan_pos), and φ < l < δ (Real.arctan_lt_self). By Real.cos_arctan and Real.sin_arctan, cos φ = 1/√(1 + l²) and sin φ = l/√(1 + l²), hence t·cos φ = 1 and t·sin φ = l, and t•(cos φ•a + sin φ•e) = (t cos φ)•a + (t sin φ)•e = a + l•e. By the hypothesis (with these t, φ), HasMassDensity C y k for y := a + l•e: k ≥ 0 and the quotients q(ρ) := C.massOn(B_ρ(y))/(ω_2·ofReal(ρ²)) tend to ofReal(k) as ρ → 0⁺ (filter 𝓝[>] 0).
3. (Suppose y ∉ spt C.) Fix R ∈ IMRep(univ, 2) with R.Represents C (IsIntegerMultiplicity C). Apply the accepted lemma `Submission.dimred_im_mass_measure` (P, n := 2, U := univ, T := C, R; univ is open): (a) C.massOn W = R.measure W for every open W; (b) for x ∈ univ, x ∈ spt C iff R.measure(B_ε(x)) ≠ 0 for every ε > 0. Since y ∈ univ and y ∉ spt C, (b) gives ε > 0 with R.measure(B_ε(y)) = 0. For 0 < ρ < ε, by (a) and monotonicity, C.massOn(B_ρ(y)) = R.measure(B_ρ(y)) ≤ R.measure(B_ε(y)) = 0, so q(ρ) = 0/(ω_2·ofReal(ρ²)) = 0 (ENNReal.zero_div).
4. (Contradiction.) The interval (0, ε) belongs to 𝓝[>] 0, so q is eventually 0 along 𝓝[>] 0 and q → 0. The filter 𝓝[>] 0 on ℝ is non-trivial and [0, ∞] is Hausdorff, so limits are unique: ofReal(k) = 0, i.e. (k : ℝ) ≤ 0, contradicting k ≥ 1. Hence y = a + l•e ∈ spt C, for every 0 < l < l₀. ∎
(Remark, an equivalent route for steps 3–4 that uses only the definitions: if y ∉ spt C = univ \ zeroRegion C, then y lies in an open W on which C vanishes (C(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ⊆ W); choose ε > 0 with B_ε(y) ⊆ W; for 0 < ρ < ε every mass-admissible form for B_ρ(y) has support in W, so every value ofReal(C ω) in the supremum defining C.massOn(B_ρ(y)) is 0 and C.massOn(B_ρ(y)) = 0; then conclude as in step 4.)
proof_key_steps: l₀ := δ; for 0 < l < δ, t := √(1+l²), φ := arctan l ∈ (0, δ) satisfy t(cos φ a + sin φ e) = a + l e.
Hence HasMassDensity C (a + l e) k with k ≥ 1.
If a + l e ∉ spt C, dimred_im_mass_measure gives massOn(B_ρ) = 0 for small ρ, so the density limit would be 0 ≠ ofReal k; contradiction.

audit.reason: The polar coefficient identity works for arbitrary a and e, so no orthonormality hypothesis is missing. Taking l₀ = δ is valid. The accepted mass/support identity and uniqueness of density limits rigorously exclude positive-density points outside the support.

subproblem.title: Localization: the cusp bound with ε = 1/20 confines support points in the box to the plane and near a
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, Q a 2-dimensional linear subspace of ℝ^P (Module.finrank ℝ Q = 2), a, e ∈ Q with |a| = |e| = 1 and ⟨a, e⟩ = 0, Z ⊆ ℝ^P, s₁ > 0, π := Q.starProjection, and assume |x − πx| ≤ (1/20)·|x − a| for every x ∈ Z with |x − a| < s₁. Then there is s₀ with 0 < s₀ ≤ 1/4 such that for every s' with 0 < s' ≤ s₀ and every x ∈ Z with ⟨x, a⟩ > 0, ||x| − 1| < s', |arctan(⟨x, e⟩/⟨x, a⟩)| < s' and |x − πx| ≤ 2s₀|x| one has |x − πx| < (s'/4)|x| and |x − a| < 3s'.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (a e : Euclid P) (Z : Set (Euclid P)) (s₁ : ℝ), Module.finrank ℝ Q = 2 → a ∈ Q → e ∈ Q → ‖a‖ = 1 → ‖e‖ = 1 → inner ℝ a e = 0 → 0 < s₁ → (∀ x ∈ Z, dist x a < s₁ → ‖x - Q.starProjection x‖ ≤ 1 / 20 * dist x a) → ∃ s₀ : ℝ, 0 < s₀ ∧ s₀ ≤ 1 / 4 ∧ (∀ s' : ℝ, 0 < s' → s' ≤ s₀ → ∀ x ∈ Z, 0 < inner ℝ x a → |‖x‖ - 1| < s' → |Real.arctan (inner ℝ x e / inner ℝ x a)| < s' → ‖x - Q.starProjection x‖ ≤ 2 * s₀ * ‖x‖ → ‖x - Q.starProjection x‖ < s' / 4 * ‖x‖ ∧ dist x a < 3 * s')
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 (localization) of the parent proof, with the cusp of step 3 at ε = 1/20 as hypothesis. Notation: π := Q.starProjection, q(x) := x − πx, f(x) := arctan(⟨x, e⟩/⟨x, a⟩), |·| and ⟨·,·⟩ Euclidean, |x − a| = dist x a.
1. (F1: π in the frame (a, e).) The pair (a, e) is orthonormal, hence linearly independent, and lies in Q with dim Q = 2, so span{a, e} = Q (two independent vectors span a 2-dimensional space; Submodule.eq_of_le_of_finrank_eq). For every x, πx ∈ Q and x − πx ⊥ Q (orthogonal projection), so ⟨πx, a⟩ = ⟨x, a⟩, ⟨πx, e⟩ = ⟨x, e⟩, and expanding πx ∈ span{a, e} in the orthonormal pair gives πx = ⟨x, a⟩a + ⟨x, e⟩e. (Equivalently: y := ⟨x, a⟩a + ⟨x, e⟩e lies in Q and ⟨x − y, w⟩ = 0 for every w = αa + βe ∈ span{a, e} = Q, so y = πx by Submodule.eq_starProjection_of_mem_of_inner_eq_zero.) Also π and q are linear, ⟨q(x), πx⟩ = 0 (Submodule.starProjection_inner_eq_zero, as πx ∈ Q), and hence |x|² = |πx + q(x)|² = |πx|² + |q(x)|² (Pythagoras: norm_add_sq_eq_norm_sq_add_norm_sq_of_inner_eq_zero; or norm_sq_eq_add_norm_sq_starProjection).
2. (Choice of s₀.) Let s₀ := min(1/4, s₁/6). Then 0 < s₀ ≤ 1/4 and 6s₀ ≤ s₁, hence 5s₀ < s₁ (as s₀ > 0).
3. (Setting.) Fix s' with 0 < s' ≤ s₀ and x ∈ Z with ⟨x, a⟩ > 0, ||x| − 1| < s', |f(x)| < s' and |q(x)| ≤ 2s₀|x|. Then |x| > 1 − s' ≥ 1 − 1/4 = 3/4 > 0. Put η := |q(x)|/|x|; then 0 ≤ η ≤ 2s₀ ≤ 1/2, hence η² ≤ η/2.
4. (Normalization.) Let x̂ := x/|x|, so |x̂| = 1, πx̂ = πx/|x|, q(x̂) = q(x)/|x| and |q(x̂)| = η. Also ⟨x̂, a⟩ = ⟨x, a⟩/|x| > 0 and u := ⟨x̂, e⟩/⟨x̂, a⟩ = ⟨x, e⟩/⟨x, a⟩, so f(x) = arctan u. By Pythagoras |πx̂|² = |x̂|² − |q(x̂)|² = 1 − η², so |πx̂| = √(1 − η²) ≤ 1, and since 0 ≤ 1 − η² ≤ 1, √(1 − η²) ≥ 1 − η².
5. (Direction of πx̂.) Let v := cos f(x)·a + sin f(x)·e; |v|² = cos² + sin² = 1. By Real.cos_arctan and Real.sin_arctan, v = (a + u e)/√(1 + u²). By (F1), πx̂ = ⟨x̂, a⟩a + ⟨x̂, e⟩e = ⟨x̂, a⟩(a + u e), and |πx̂|² = ⟨x̂, a⟩² + ⟨x̂, e⟩² = ⟨x̂, a⟩²(1 + u²), so |πx̂| = ⟨x̂, a⟩√(1 + u²) (⟨x̂, a⟩ > 0). Therefore πx̂ = |πx̂|·v.
6. (Three estimates.) (a) |πx̂ − v| = |(|πx̂| − 1)v| = 1 − |πx̂| ≤ 1 − (1 − η²) = η². (b) |v − a|² = (cos f − 1)² + sin² f = 2 − 2cos f ≤ f² because cos f ≥ 1 − f²/2 (Real.one_sub_sq_div_two_le_cos), where f := f(x); so |v − a| ≤ |f(x)| < s'. (c) |q(x̂)| = η.
7. (Distance to a.) Since x̂ = πx̂ + q(x̂), x̂ − a = (πx̂ − v) + (v − a) + q(x̂), so |x̂ − a| < η² + s' + η ≤ s' + (3/2)η. Also x − x̂ = (|x| − 1)x̂, so |x − x̂| = ||x| − 1| < s'. Hence |x − a| ≤ |x − x̂| + |x̂ − a| < 2s' + (3/2)η.
8. (Apply the cusp bound.) Since s' ≤ s₀ and η ≤ 2s₀: |x − a| < 2s₀ + 3s₀ = 5s₀ < s₁. As x ∈ Z, the hypothesis gives |q(x)| ≤ (1/20)|x − a| < (2s' + (3/2)η)/20 = s'/10 + (3/40)η.
9. (Solve for η.) As |x| > 3/4 and η ≥ 0: (3/4)η ≤ η|x| = |q(x)| < s'/10 + (3/40)η, so (27/40)η < s'/10, i.e. η < (4/27)s'.
10. (Conclusions.) |q(x)| = η|x| < (4/27)s'|x| ≤ (s'/4)|x| (as |x| > 0, s' > 0 and 4/27 < 1/4), and |x − a| < 2s' + (3/2)(4/27)s' = 2s' + (2/9)s' < 3s'. These are the two asserted inequalities, for every admissible s' and x. ∎
proof_key_steps: πx = ⟨x,a⟩a + ⟨x,e⟩e and |x|² = |πx|² + |q(x)|² (orthonormal frame of the 2-plane Q).
s₀ := min(1/4, s₁/6), so 5s₀ < s₁.
With η := |q(x)|/|x| ≤ 1/2 and v := cos f a + sin f e: πx̂ = |πx̂|v, |πx̂ − v| ≤ η², |v − a| ≤ |f| < s', so |x − a| < 2s' + 1.5η ≤ 5s₀ < s₁.

audit.reason: The proof establishes the projection formula and every normalization identity under the stated hypotheses. The choice s₀ = min(1/4, s₁/6) permits applying the cusp bound, which gives η < 4s'/27 and both claimed strict inequalities. The constants and strictness are correct.

subproblem.title: Two orthonormal frames of the same 2-plane: equal spans and 2-covectors agree up to a sign
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, Q a linear subspace of ℝ^P with dim Q = 2 (Module.finrank ℝ Q = 2), a, e ∈ Q with |a| = |e| = 1 and ⟨a, e⟩ = 0, and τ = (τ_0, τ_1) an orthonormal pair in ℝ^P (τ : Fin 2 → Euclid P) with a, e ∈ span{τ_0, τ_1}. Then span{τ_0, τ_1} = Q, and there is ε ∈ ℤ with |ε| = 1 (ε.natAbs = 1) such that α(τ) = ε·α(a, e) for every 2-covector α ∈ Covector(ℝ^P, 2), where α(a, e) denotes α applied to ![a, e].
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (a e : Euclid P) (τ : Fin 2 → Euclid P), Module.finrank ℝ Q = 2 → a ∈ Q → e ∈ Q → ‖a‖ = 1 → ‖e‖ = 1 → inner ℝ a e = 0 → Orthonormal ℝ τ → a ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ) → e ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ) → Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ) = Q ∧ ∃ ε : ℤ, ε.natAbs = 1 ∧ ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) 2, α τ = (ε : ℝ) * α ![a, e]
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the end of step 2(d) (Q = span{a, e} ⊆ Q' and equal dimensions give Q' = Q) and step 2(e) (orientation: α(τ) = det(O)·α(a, e)) of the parent proof. Notation: Q' := span{τ_0, τ_1} = Submodule.span ℝ (range τ), W := span{a, e}.
1. (dim Q' = 2.) τ is orthonormal, hence linearly independent (Orthonormal.linearIndependent), so finrank Q' = card(Fin 2) = 2 (finrank_span_eq_card).
2. (dim W = 2.) The pair ![a, e] is orthonormal (|a| = |e| = 1, ⟨a, e⟩ = 0, hence also ⟨e, a⟩ = 0), hence linearly independent, so finrank W = 2.
3. (Q' = Q.) W ≤ Q because a, e ∈ Q, and finrank W = 2 = finrank Q; since Q is finite-dimensional, W = Q (Submodule.eq_of_le_of_finrank_eq). Likewise W ≤ Q' because a, e ∈ Q' (hypothesis), and finrank W = 2 = finrank Q', so W = Q'. Hence Q' = W = Q, the first claim.
4. (Coordinates of τ.) For i ∈ {0, 1}, τ_i ∈ Q' = W = span{a, e}, so τ_i = x_i·a + y_i·e for some reals x_i, y_i (Submodule.mem_span_pair). Write p := x_0, q := y_0, r := x_1, s := y_1.

subproblem.title: The flat current c[[span τ]] has an integer multiplicity representation with measure |c|·Hⁿ⌞span τ
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let τ = (τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}) be an orthonormal family in ℝ^P (τ : Fin n → Euclid P, Orthonormal ℝ τ), let Q' := span{τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}} (Submodule.span ℝ (range τ)) and let c ∈ ℤ with c ≠ 0. Then there is an integer multiplicity triple R ∈ IMRep(ℝ^P, n) (IMRep univ n) such that (i) R.action ω = c·∫_{Q'} ω(x)(τ) dHⁿ(x) for every ambient n-form ω : ℝ^P → Covector(ℝ^P, n) (DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n), where Hⁿ := μHE[n] and ω(x)(τ) is the covector ω(x) evaluated at the n-tuple τ; and (ii) R.measure = |c|·Hⁿ⌞Q', i.e. R.measure = (c.natAbs : ℝ≥0∞) • μHE[n].restrict Q'.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 2(a) of the parent proof (the representation R' = (Q', m, ξ') of the tangent cone c[[Q']]), stated for a general orthonormal n-tuple. Notation: ℝ^P := Euclid P, Hⁿ := μHE[n], Q' := span(range τ), m := |c| = c.natAbs ∈ ℕ, s := sgn(c) = Int.sign c.
1. (Integers.) Since c ≠ 0, m ≥ 1 and s ∈ {1, −1}, and s·m = c (Int.sign_mul_natAbs); in particular (m : ℝ)·((s : ℝ)·y) = (c : ℝ)·y for every real y.
2. (Dimension and closedness of Q'.) An orthonormal family is linearly independent (Orthonormal.linearIndependent), so finrank Q' = card(Fin n) = n (finrank_span_eq_card). Q' is a finite-dimensional subspace of ℝ^P, hence closed (Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional), hence a Borel set (IsClosed.measurableSet).
3. (A parametrization.) Define ι : Euclid n → ℝ^P by ι(v) := Σ_{i} v_i·τ_i (v_i := v i). ι is linear. By orthonormality, |ι(v)|² = Σ_{i,j} v_i v_j⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩ = Σ_i v_i² = |v|², so |ι(v) − ι(v')| = |ι(v − v')| = |v − v'|: ι is an isometry, in particular 1-Lipschitz, and ι(0) = 0. Its range is Q': every ι(v) is a linear combination of the τ_i, so lies in Q'; conversely range ι is a linear subspace (image of a linear map) containing every τ_i = ι(e_i) (e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1), hence contains span(range τ) = Q'. (Equivalently: range of Fintype.linearCombination ℝ τ is span(range τ).)
4. (Rectifiability.) By SimonGMT `countablyRectifiable_range` applied to the Lipschitz map ι : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ^P, the set Q' = range ι is countably n-rectifiable (CountablyRectifiable n Q').
5. (Local finiteness.) Let K ⊆ ℝ^P be compact. By `Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_preimage` (ι an isometry), Hⁿ(K ∩ range ι) = Hⁿ(ι⁻¹(K)), where on the right Hⁿ = μHE[n] on Euclid n, which equals Lebesgue measure `volume` (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). K is bounded, say K ⊆ closedBall(0, ρ); for v ∈ ι⁻¹(K), |v| = |ι(v)| ≤ ρ, so ι⁻¹(K) ⊆ closedBall(0, ρ) ⊆ Euclid n, a compact set of finite Lebesgue measure. Hence Hⁿ(Q' ∩ K) < ∞, and ∫⁻_{Q'∩K} (m : [0,∞]) dHⁿ = m·Hⁿ(Q' ∩ K) < ∞ (lintegral of a constant).
6. (The orientation.) Let E_τ : Covector(ℝ^P, n) → ℝ, E_τ(α) := α(τ). It is linear in α, and |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖·Π_i|τ_i| = ‖α‖ (operator-norm bound for continuous alternating maps), so E_τ is a continuous linear map, i.e. an element of MultiVector P n = (Covector(ℝ^P, n) →L[ℝ] ℝ); in Mathlib it is `ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply ℝ (Euclid P) ℝ τ`. Put ξ := s·E_τ ∈ MultiVector P n, so ξ(α) = s·α(τ).
7. (The triple.) Define R by carrier := Q' (as a set), mult(x) := m for all x, orient(x) := ξ for all x. Check the fields of IMRep(univ, n):
 (a) measurableSet_carrier: step 2.
 (b) carrier_subset: Q' ⊆ univ.
 (c) rectifiable: step 4.
 (d) measurable_mult: a constant function is measurable.
 (e) mult_pos: for x ∈ Q', mult(x) = m ≥ 1 > 0 (step 1).
 (f) locallyIntegrable_mult: for compact K ⊆ univ, ∫⁻_{Q'∩K} m dHⁿ ≠ ∞ by step 5.
 (g) aestronglyMeasurable_orient: a constant function is (a.e.) strongly measurable.
 (h) orients: we show the property for every x ∈ Q'; since Q' is measurable this gives it for Hⁿ⌞Q'-a.e. x (ae_restrict_of_forall_mem). Fix x ∈ Q' and take the subspace Q'. HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n Q' x Q' holds by SimonGMT `hasApproximateTangentSpaceAt_submodule` (finrank Q' = n by step 2, x ∈ Q'). IsUnitOrientationOf (orient x) Q' holds with witness τ: τ is orthonormal, span(range τ) = Q', and if c > 0 then s = 1 and orient(x)(α) = α(τ) for all α (left disjunct), while if c < 0 then s = −1 and orient(x)(α) = −α(τ) for all α (right disjunct).
8. (Action.) For every ambient n-form ω, by definition R.action ω = ∫_{Q'} (mult(x) : ℝ)·orient(x)(ω(x)) dHⁿ(x) = ∫_{Q'} (m : ℝ)·(s·ω(x)(τ)) dHⁿ(x) = ∫_{Q'} c·ω(x)(τ) dHⁿ(x) (pointwise identity of step 1) = c·∫_{Q'} ω(x)(τ) dHⁿ(x) by `integral_const_mul`, which holds for every function (no integrability is needed). This is (i).
9. (Measure.) R.measure = (Hⁿ⌞Q').withDensity(x ↦ (m : [0,∞])) by definition of IMRep.measure, and a constant density gives (Hⁿ⌞Q').withDensity(fun _ ↦ m) = m • Hⁿ⌞Q' (`withDensity_const`). This is (ii), with m = (c.natAbs : ℝ≥0∞). ∎

ι(v) = Σ v_i τ_i is a linear isometry Euclid n → ℝ^P with range Q'; hence Q' is countably n-rectifiable (countablyRectifiable_range).
Hⁿ(Q' ∩ K) = volume(ι⁻¹K) < ∞ for compact K (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_preimage, euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume).
orient ≡ s·(α ↦ α(τ)) is a constant MultiVector; every x ∈ Q' has approximate tangent space Q' (hasApproximateTangentSpaceAt_submodule) oriented by ±τ.
R.action ω = ∫_{Q'} m·s·ω(x)(τ) = c∫_{Q'} ω(x)(τ) (integral_const_mul); R.measure = m • Hⁿ⌞Q' (withDensity_const).

subproblem.title: Rescaled points with a uniform lower mass bound converge into the support of the vague limit
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, μ a measure on ℝ^P with μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P, S ⊆ ℝ^P closed, a, w ∈ ℝ^P, m ∈ ℝ, (λ_j)_{j∈ℕ} with λ_j > 0 and (w_j)_{j∈ℕ} in ℝ^P with w_j → w. Assume (V) for every continuous compactly supported g : ℝ^P → ℝ, λ_j^{−2}·∫ g(dilation a λ_j x) dμ(x) → m·∫_S g dH² (H² := μHE[2]); and (L) for every r > 0 and all sufficiently large j, ω_2·(λ_j r)² ≤ μ(B_{λ_j r}(a + λ_j w_j)) in [0, ∞], i.e. unitBallVolume 2 * ENNReal.ofReal ((λ_j r)^2) ≤ μ (ball (a + λ_j • w_j) (λ_j r)). Then w ∈ S.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (S : Set (Euclid P)) (a w : Euclid P) (m : ℝ) (lams : ℕ → ℝ) (ws : ℕ → Euclid P), IsClosed S → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → μ K ≠ ∞) → (∀ j, 0 < lams j) → Tendsto ws atTop (𝓝 w) → (∀ g : Euclid P → ℝ, Continuous g → HasCompactSupport g → Tendsto (fun j => (lams j)⁻¹ ^ 2 * ∫ x, g (dilation a (lams j) x) ∂μ) atTop (𝓝 (m * ∫ x in S, g x ∂μHE[2]))) → (∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → ∀ᶠ j in atTop, unitBallVolume 2 * ENNReal.ofReal ((lams j * r) ^ 2) ≤ μ (ball (a + lams j • ws j) (lams j * r))) → w ∈ S
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the common core of steps 2(d) and 3 of the parent proof (the test functions g_{w,r}, the inclusion of a small ball around a + λ_j w_j in η_j⁻¹ of a ball around w, the lower bound ω_2 r² for the rescaled integrals, and closedness). Notation: η_j := dilation a λ_j, so η_j(x) = −λ_j^{−1}a + λ_j^{−1}x = λ_j^{−1}(x − a); ω_2 := unitBallVolume 2 = volume(B_1(0) ⊆ Euclid 2); A_j(g) := λ_j^{−2}∫ g(η_j(x)) dμ(x).
1. (ω_2.) The open unit ball of Euclid 2 is nonempty and open, so it has positive Lebesgue measure (measure_ball_pos); it is bounded, so it has finite measure (measure_ball_lt_top). Hence κ := ω_2.toReal > 0, and for t ≥ 0, (ω_2·ofReal(t)).toReal = κ·t.
2. (Assume the contrary.) Suppose w ∉ S. As S is closed, its complement is open, so there is ρ > 0 with B_ρ(w) ∩ S = ∅. Put r := ρ/4 > 0 and g(z) := min(1, max(0, 2 − |z − w|/(2r))). Then g is continuous, 0 ≤ g ≤ 1, g(z) = 1 if |z − w| ≤ 2r, and g(z) = 0 if |z − w| ≥ 4r = ρ. Hence the support of g lies in closedBall(w, ρ), which is compact (ℝ^P is proper), so g has compact support; and g = 0 on S (points of S satisfy |z − w| ≥ ρ). Therefore ∫_S g dH² = 0 (setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero), and (V) gives A_j(g) → m·0 = 0.
3. (Integrability.) η_j is a homeomorphism of ℝ^P (affine with linear part λ_j^{−1}·id, λ_j ≠ 0), so g∘η_j is continuous with compact support (support ⊆ η_j⁻¹(tsupport g), compact). Since μ is finite on compact sets (IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ), g∘η_j is μ-integrable (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport). Put B_j := B_{λ_j r}(a + λ_j w_j); B_j ⊆ closedBall(a + λ_j w_j, λ_j r), compact, so μ(B_j) < ∞ and the indicator 1_{B_j} is μ-integrable.
4. (Lower bound for large j.) By w_j → w and (L) (with this r), there is J such that for all j ≥ J: |w_j − w| < r and ω_2·ofReal((λ_j r)²) ≤ μ(B_j). Fix j ≥ J. For x ∈ B_j, η_j(x) − w_j = λ_j^{−1}(x − (a + λ_j w_j)), so |η_j(x) − w_j| < λ_j^{−1}·λ_j r = r, hence |η_j(x) − w| < 2r and g(η_j(x)) = 1. Since g ≥ 0 everywhere, 1_{B_j} ≤ g∘η_j pointwise, and integral monotonicity (both integrable, step 3) gives μ(B_j).toReal = ∫ 1_{B_j} dμ ≤ ∫ g∘η_j dμ. As μ(B_j) < ∞, monotonicity of ENNReal.toReal on finite values (ENNReal.toReal_mono) applied to ω_2·ofReal((λ_j r)²) ≤ μ(B_j) gives μ(B_j).toReal ≥ (ω_2·ofReal((λ_j r)²)).toReal = κλ_j²r² (step 1). Multiplying by λ_j^{−2} > 0: A_j(g) ≥ κ r² for every j ≥ J.
5. (Contradiction.) Passing to the limit in A_j(g) ≥ κr² (j ≥ J) gives 0 = lim A_j(g) ≥ κr² > 0 (ge_of_tendsto), which is impossible. Hence w ∈ S. ∎
proof_key_steps: If w ∉ S pick a bump g = 1 on closedBall(w, 2r), 0 off B_{4r}(w), with B_{4r}(w) ∩ S = ∅; then ∫_S g dH² = 0 and (V) forces λ_j^{−2}∫ g∘η_j dμ → 0.
For large j, |w_j − w| < r and η_j maps B_{λ_j r}(a + λ_j w_j) into B_{2r}(w), so ∫ g∘η_j dμ ≥ μ(B_{λ_j r}(a + λ_j w_j)) ≥ κλ_j²r² by (L).
Hence λ_j^{−2}∫ g∘η_j dμ ≥ κr² > 0 eventually, contradicting the limit 0; so w ∈ S.

subproblem.title: Blow-ups converging in mass to c[[span τ]]: the pulled-back mass measures converge vaguely to |c|·Hⁿ⌞span τ
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n), a ∈ ℝ^P, (λ_j)_{j∈ℕ} with λ_j > 0, C' ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P), τ : Fin n → ℝ^P orthonormal with Q' := span(range τ), and c ∈ ℤ with c ≠ 0, such that C'(ω) = c·∫_{Q'} ω(x)(τ) dHⁿ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) (TestFormOn univ n, Hⁿ := μHE[n]) and MassMeasuresConverge (j ↦ blowUp C a λ_j) C' holds. Then for every integer multiplicity representation R ∈ IMRep(ℝ^P, n) of C and every continuous compactly supported g : ℝ^P → ℝ, λ_j^{−n}·∫ g(η_j(x)) dR.measure(x) → |c|·∫_{Q'} g dHⁿ as j → ∞, where η_j := dilation a λ_j (η_j(x) = λ_j^{−1}(x − a)).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (a : Euclid P) (lams : ℕ → ℝ) (hlams : ∀ j, 0 < lams j) (C' : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (τ : Fin n → Euclid P) (c : ℤ), Orthonormal ℝ τ → c ≠ 0 → (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, C' ω = (c : ℝ) * ∫ x in (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ) : Set (Euclid P)), (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x τ ∂μHE[n]) → MassMeasuresConverge (fun j => blowUp C a (lams j) (hlams j).ne') C' → ∀ R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, R.Represents C → ∀ g : Euclid P → ℝ, Continuous g → HasCompactSupport g → Tendsto (fun j => (lams j)⁻¹ ^ n * ∫ x, g (dilation a (lams j) x) ∂R.measure) atTop (𝓝 ((c.natAbs : ℝ) * ∫ x in (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ) : Set (Euclid P)), g x ∂μHE[n]))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2(a)–2(c) of the parent proof (representation of the limit, representations of the blow-ups, vague convergence (V)), for general n. Notation: Hⁿ := μHE[n], Q' := span(range τ), C_j := blowUp C a λ_j (hλ_j ≠ 0), η_j := dilation a λ_j, so η_j(x) = −λ_j^{−1}a + λ_j^{−1}x = λ_j^{−1}(x − a). Fix R ∈ IMRep(univ, n) with R.Represents C and a continuous g : ℝ^P → ℝ with compact support.
1. (A representation of C'.) By the sibling `Submission.idtp_cse_etp_plane_imrep` (P, n, τ, c; τ orthonormal, c ≠ 0) there is R' ∈ IMRep(univ, n) with R'.action ω = c·∫_{Q'} ω(x)(τ) dHⁿ for every ambient n-form ω, and R'.measure = (|c| : [0,∞])·Hⁿ⌞Q'. For every test form ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P), the hypothesis gives C'(ω) = c·∫_{Q'} ω(x)(τ) dHⁿ = R'.action ω, so R'.Represents C'. Moreover ∫ g dR'.measure = ((|c| : [0,∞]).toReal)·∫_{Q'} g dHⁿ = |c|·∫_{Q'} g dHⁿ (`integral_smul_measure`; toReal of a natural number cast is that number).
2. (Representations of the blow-ups.) For each j apply the accepted lemma `Submission.dtc_blowUp_imrep` with P, n, U := univ, T := C, x := a, lam := λ_j, hlam := (λ_j > 0) and the representation R: it gives R_j ∈ IMRep(dilation a λ_j '' univ, n) with R_j.Represents C_j (C_j = blowUp C a λ_j (hλ_j).ne', exactly the j-th current in the hypothesis MassMeasuresConverge) and R_j.measure(B) = ofReal(λ_j^{−n})·R.measure(η_j⁻¹(B)) for every measurable B. Choose such an R_j for every j (choice), obtaining a family (R_j)_j with R_j.Represents C_j for all j.
3. (Push-forward formula.) Fix j. η_j is continuous (affine), hence measurable. For every measurable B, (ofReal(λ_j^{−n})·(η_j)_#R.measure)(B) = ofReal(λ_j^{−n})·R.measure(η_j⁻¹(B)) = R_j.measure(B) (Measure.map_apply, smul_apply). Two measures that agree on all measurable sets are equal (Measure.ext), so R_j.measure = ofReal(λ_j^{−n})•(η_j)_#R.measure. Since g is continuous it is strongly measurable, so ∫ g dR_j.measure = (ofReal(λ_j^{−n})).toReal·∫ g d(η_j)_#R.measure (integral_smul_measure) = λ_j^{−n}·∫ g(η_j(x)) dR.measure(x) (integral_map with η_j measurable and g a.e.-strongly measurable; toReal(ofReal t) = t for t = λ_j^{−n} ≥ 0). Both identities hold without any integrability assumption.
4. (Vague convergence.) Apply MassMeasuresConverge (j ↦ C_j) C' to the family (R_j) (step 2), to R' (step 1, R'.Represents C') and to f := g (continuous, compactly supported, tsupport g ⊆ univ): ∫ g dR_j.measure → ∫ g dR'.measure. By steps 3 and 1 this says λ_j^{−n}·∫ g(η_j(x)) dR.measure(x) → |c|·∫_{Q'} g dHⁿ. ∎
proof_key_steps: plane_imrep gives R' representing C' with ∫ g dR'.measure = |c|∫_{Q'} g dHⁿ.
dtc_blowUp_imrep gives, for each j, R_j representing blowUp C a λ_j with R_j.measure = ofReal(λ_j^{−n})•(η_j)_#R.measure.
∫ g dR_j.measure = λ_j^{−n}∫ g∘η_j dR.measure (integral_smul_measure, integral_map).
MassMeasuresConverge applied to (R_j), R', g yields the limit.

subproblem.title: Cusp lemma: if every blow-up of μ at a is (vaguely) a multiple of H²⌞Q, support points near a satisfy |x − πx| ≤ ε|x − a|
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, μ a measure on ℝ^P with μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K, Z ⊆ ℝ^P, Q a linear subspace of ℝ^P, a ∈ Q, m ∈ ℝ, and π := Q.starProjection (orthogonal projection onto Q). Assume (i) ω_2ρ² ≤ μ(B_ρ(y)) (unitBallVolume 2 * ENNReal.ofReal (ρ^2) ≤ μ (ball y ρ)) for every y ∈ Z and every ρ > 0; and (ii) for every sequence λ_j > 0 with λ_j → 0 there is a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ such that λ_{φ(j)}^{−2}·∫ g(dilation a λ_{φ(j)} x) dμ(x) → m·∫_Q g dH² (H² := μHE[2]) for every continuous compactly supported g : ℝ^P → ℝ. Then for every ε > 0 there is s > 0 such that |x − πx| ≤ ε·|x − a| for every x ∈ Z with |x − a| < s.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (Z : Set (Euclid P)) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (a : Euclid P) (m : ℝ), a ∈ Q → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → μ K ≠ ∞) → (∀ y ∈ Z, ∀ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ → unitBallVolume 2 * ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ 2) ≤ μ (ball y ρ)) → (∀ lams : ℕ → ℝ, (∀ j, 0 < lams j) → Tendsto lams atTop (𝓝 0) → ∃ φ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono φ ∧ ∀ g : Euclid P → ℝ, Continuous g → HasCompactSupport g → Tendsto (fun j => (lams (φ j))⁻¹ ^ 2 * ∫ x, g (dilation a (lams (φ j)) x) ∂μ) atTop (𝓝 (m * ∫ x in (Q : Set (Euclid P)), g x ∂μHE[2]))) → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ s : ℝ, 0 < s ∧ ∀ x ∈ Z, dist x a < s → ‖x - Q.starProjection x‖ ≤ ε * dist x a
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 (the cusp) of the parent proof, with the blow-up input (V) and the lower bound abstracted into hypotheses (ii) and (i). Notation: π := Q.starProjection, q(x) := x − πx, |x − a| = dist x a.
1. (q.) q = id − π is a continuous linear map ℝ^P → ℝ^P. Since a ∈ Q, πa = a (Submodule.starProjection_eq_self_iff), so q(a) = 0 and q(x − a) = q(x) for every x. Q is finite-dimensional, hence closed (Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional).
2. (Assume the contrary.) Suppose there is ε > 0 for which no s > 0 works. Then for every j ∈ ℕ (using s := 1/(j + 1)) there is x_j ∈ Z with s_j := |x_j − a| < 1/(j + 1) and |q(x_j)| > ε·s_j; choose such x_j for every j. If s_j = 0 then x_j = a and |q(x_j)| = |q(a)| = 0 = ε·s_j, which is impossible; so s_j > 0. As 0 < s_j < 1/(j + 1), s_j → 0.
3. (Blow-up subsequence.) Apply (ii) to λ_j := s_j (positive, → 0): there is φ strictly increasing such that for every continuous compactly supported g, (V_φ): s_{φ(j)}^{−2}∫ g(dilation a s_{φ(j)} x) dμ(x) → m∫_Q g dH².
4. (Compactness of directions.) Put w_j := s_{φ(j)}^{−1}(x_{φ(j)} − a). Then |w_j| = s_{φ(j)}^{−1}|x_{φ(j)} − a| = 1, so every w_j lies in the unit sphere of ℝ^P, which is compact (isCompact_sphere; ℝ^P is proper). By sequential compactness (IsCompact.tendsto_subseq) there are ψ : ℕ → ℕ strictly increasing and w with |w| = 1 such that w_{ψ(j)} → w.
5. (Hypotheses of the sibling lemma.) Put λ'_j := s_{φ(ψ(j))} > 0 and w'_j := w_{ψ(j)}, so w'_j → w. Since ψ is strictly increasing, ψ(j) → ∞ (StrictMono.tendsto_atTop), and composing the convergence (V_φ) with ψ gives, for every continuous compactly supported g: λ'_j^{−2}∫ g(dilation a λ'_j x) dμ(x) → m∫_Q g dH². Moreover, a + λ'_j w'_j = a + s·s^{−1}(x − a) = x with s := s_{φ(ψ(j))} > 0, x := x_{φ(ψ(j))} ∈ Z, so by (i) with ρ := λ'_j r > 0: ω_2·ofReal((λ'_j r)²) ≤ μ(B_{λ'_j r}(a + λ'_j w'_j)) for every r > 0 and every j (in particular for all sufficiently large j).
6. (w ∈ Q.) By the sibling `Submission.idtp_cse_etp_rescaled_limit_mem` applied to μ (finite on compacts), S := Q (closed), a, w, m, (λ'_j), (w'_j) and the hypotheses of step 5: w ∈ Q, hence q(w) = 0.
7. (Contradiction.) For each j, with s := s_{φ(ψ(j))} and x := x_{φ(ψ(j))}: |q(w'_j)| = s^{−1}|q(x − a)| = s^{−1}|q(x)| > s^{−1}·ε s = ε (steps 1, 2). Since q and |·| are continuous and w'_j → w, |q(w'_j)| → |q(w)|, so |q(w)| ≥ ε > 0 (ge_of_tendsto), contradicting q(w) = 0. Hence for every ε > 0 a suitable s > 0 exists. ∎
proof_key_steps: q = id − π is continuous linear with q(a) = 0 (a ∈ Q).
If the claim fails for ε, pick x_j ∈ Z with 0 < s_j = |x_j − a| < 1/(j+1) and |q(x_j)| > εs_j.
Use (ii) on λ_j = s_j and compactness of the unit sphere to get a subsequence with w_j = (x_j − a)/s_j → w, |q(w_j)| > ε.
a + s_j w_j = x_j ∈ Z gives the lower bound (i) at radius s_j r; rescaled_limit_mem yields w ∈ Q, so q(w) = 0, contradicting |q(w)| ≥ ε.
